html:
Latvia is a Baltic country on the eastern shore of the Baltic Sea, with Riga as its capital. Its people speak a Baltic language, close only to Lithuanian. Riga was founded by German crusaders in 1201 and was a Hanseatic trading city; German landlords dominated the countryside for centuries, under Swedish and then Russian rule.

Latvia declared independence in November 1918 and won it in a war against both Soviet Russia and German forces. In 1940 the Soviet Union occupied it under the secret terms of the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact. Germany held it from 1941 to 1944, then Soviet rule returned, with mass deportations and the settlement of many Russian speakers.

In 1989 Latvians joined Estonians and Lithuanians in the Baltic Way, a human chain across all three countries. Independence came back in 1991 as the Soviet Union broke up. Latvia joined NATO and the European Union in 2004.
